## Checklist

- [ ] **Honesty firewall** — one real data stream; no fabricated, estimated, or interpolated values shown as real.
- [ ] **No engagement dark patterns** — no streaks, leaderboards, badges, or FOMO.
- [ ] **Museum, not dashboard** — the change stays calm and editorial; it doesn't clutter or gamify.
- [ ] **Build passes** — TypeScript stays strict (no new `any`); `npm run build` is green.
- [ ] **Screenshots attached** for any UI change (both `nocturne` and `day` themes if relevant).
- [ ] **Licensing understood** — my contribution is licensed **CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0**, and any artwork I add is non-commercial (not for resale by anyone) and mine to license.

## Reviewer notes

<!--
Where should the reviewer look hardest? Which parts are a guess, an assumption,
or otherwise less certain? Most of an AI-written repository is plausible on its
face — flagging the weak spots is what makes review effective.

This is also where the review fleet's result goes (`/review`, or step 6 of
`/pick`): which agents `.github/scripts/review.sh plan` named, what they found,
what was fixed and what was dismissed and why. If the routing selected no agent,
say so — "found nothing" and "did not run" are different facts.

A file on the issue's `Must not touch` list needs a line of the exact shape

    Boundary change: <path> — issue #<n> amended, <why>

without which scope-reviewer's blocker stands.
-->
